A sport with
a long breath.

Vayu is the Sanskrit word for wind. Ta names the thing that travels. Together, VAYUTA is a name for an object that lets you see the invisible.

For generations, play has been a way to study the world: weight, balance, patience, and the space between one gesture and the next.

VAYUTA carries that old intelligence into the present. A square cloth body is framed with four triangular tabs, weighted at the tips, and held by a central grip. When it turns, the geometry opens into a moving compass — part sport, part meditation, part conversation.

Every VAYUTA is reversible: one print on each face, stitched around a balanced center so it can glide from either side. No batteries. No light show. Just fabric, air, and the skill you build by returning to the same motion until it becomes your own.

own orbit.

VAYUTA rewards attention. The shape gives you a clear visual cue, while the soft construction gives your hands room to make mistakes safely. Start close to the body; let the circle grow as your control grows.

the beginner's guide

Learn the first
three minutes.

Give yourself a little space: a clear floor, soft light, and enough room to extend your arm without touching anything. Shoes optional. Curiosity required.

↗Keep the central grip facing your palm. The four tabs should travel beside you, not straight into the floor.
01

Wake the cloth

Hold the central grip lightly between thumb and forefinger. Let one tab hang. Draw a small circle with your wrist and allow the fabric to follow.

02

Build a plane

Make the circle wider from your elbow, then your shoulder. Keep the motion smooth and relaxed. The goal is an even plane, not speed.

03

Change direction

Slow the circle until you can feel the weight return. Reverse with a small inward turn of your wrist. Practice both sides for balance.

04

Find your phrase

Add a pause, a wrap, a pass from hand to hand, or a turn of your body. Your first sequence is simply three movements you enjoy repeating.

Practice library

Build a clean circle

Repeat each movement for eight slow counts before joining them together.

  • pendulum start
  • side plane
  • reverse with control

Connect the tabs

Keep the fabric moving while you change the relationship between your hand, shoulder, and body.

  • wrap and unwrap
  • hand-to-hand pass
  • pause and resume

Write a moving phrase

Use timing, direction, and level changes to make a one-minute sequence that feels like yours.

  • continuous reverse
  • body tracing
  • performance phrase

the VAYUTA world circuit

Bring your
best circle.

A worldwide celebration of movement, craft, and the many ways people make a soft object sing. Local gatherings lead to an annual open competition with space for beginners, artists, and technical flow practitioners.

2027first open season
Everywherecities · studios · fields

How the day works

  1. 01Open practice: arrive, meet your circle, and warm up.
  2. 02One-minute round: show control, rhythm, and a clear beginning.
  3. 03Open expression: your own phrase, your own colors, your own pace.
  4. 04Craft award: a celebration of the most thoughtful VAYUTA design.
  5. 05Pass it on: every finalist teaches one movement to someone new.
